reference.title: Barbell Standing Leg Calf Raise
reference.listing: Video (title and product number from the listing URL; the page itself could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the heels rise, inhale as they lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, 0.8 s pause, 1.8 s down

prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight that leaves about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8) with a full rise every rep.
prescription.progression: Heavier bar, then the balls of the feet on a low step for a deeper stretch.

cues.text: Bar on the upper traps, hands just outside the shoulders, shoulder blades squeezed. Feet hip width, toes forward, knees straight but soft.
Push through the balls of the feet and lift both heels as high as you can, ankles straight up, body tall.
Pause at the top and squeeze the calves.
Lower the heels slowly all the way to the floor.
Heels down, re-brace before the next rep.

mistakes.fix: Lower under control and pause briefly with the heels down.
Press through the big-toe side; keep the ankles in line with the knees.
Keep the knees straight but soft the whole rep.
Stand tall; the body rises straight up over the balls of the feet.

kinematics.norm: Full heel rise, about 30-40 degrees of plantarflexion past neutral (clinical opinion)
As high as the ankle allows (clinical opinion)
High bar on the upper trapezius; centre of mass over the balls of the feet at the top (common coaching)
Pause at the top, slow lowering (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Barbell Standing Leg Calf Raise, video (movement reference only)
Hébert-Losier, Schneiders, García, Sullivan & Simoneau 2012, influence of knee flexion angle and age on triceps surae muscle fatigue during heel raises (J Strength Cond Res 26(11))
Kinoshita, Maeo et al. 2023, triceps surae muscle hypertrophy is greater after standing versus seated calf-raise training (Front Physiol 14:1272106)

cautions: Take the bar from a rack at about shoulder height and re-rack it after the set; the rack drawn here shows only the J-hooks.
Balance limits the load: stand near the rack or use a light bar first.
Keep the bar on the muscle of the upper back, never on the neck.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Achilles or calf pain: smaller range, slower lowering, lighter bar.
Balance issues: dumbbell calf raise with one hand on support.
regressions: Single-leg dumbbell calf raise with a hand on the wall.
progressions: Balls of the feet on a low step for a deeper stretch.
Barbell standing single leg calf raise.

muscleNotes.calves_r: Gastrocnemius and soleus lift the heels; with the knees straight the gastrocnemius shares more of the work (Hébert-Losier 2012); standing calf raises grew the gastrocnemius more than seated ones (Kinoshita 2023).
muscleNotes.calves_l: Gastrocnemius and soleus lift the heels; with the knees straight the gastrocnemius shares more of the work (Hébert-Losier 2012); standing calf raises grew the gastrocnemius more than seated ones (Kinoshita 2023).
